properties.statement: Built a Python harness that drives the built binary over stdio JSON-RPC and runs a scripted PLAN of tool calls against an ISOLATED COPY of the design — copy seeded by importing the committed export into a fresh store, with an assertion refusing any path that resolves to the live store — recording every call, reply, refusal and latency to JSONL for later analysis. Used it for 430 calls exercising all 180 served tools, in tranches: predict from the published schema, call, diff prediction against outcome, then re-run the failures with values read from the schema instead of guessed. Nothing served does this: there is no way to ask reflow2 to exercise its own surface, no way to run a batch of calls against a scratch copy of a design, and no way to get a machine-readable record of what a call returned. The two things that come closest answer different questions — one finds a tool by description, the other reports what a session did by hand. The sweep's central measurement (guessing enum values refused 13 of 20 constructors; reading the published schema refused 0) is only obtainable by actually issuing both sets of calls, so the harness was the instrument, not a convenience.
